issues.finding: The system is written Log{2i}, which is not the named sequent calculus in this section; the claim and cross-references concern G2i.
issues.proposed_resolution: Name G2i in the opening claim.

issues.location: first corollary about translating G2i proofs
issues.finding: The corollary omits the cut-free premise required for the asserted normality, names N2c instead of N2i, and leaves C undefined when the G2i succedent is empty.
issues.proposed_resolution: Restrict the claim to cut-free G2i proofs, name N2i, and define C as the succedent formula or falsity when the succedent is empty.

issues.finding: The conditional sentence omits the property of the starting N2i proof that makes cut avoidance possible.
issues.proposed_resolution: State that the starting N2i proof is normal.

issues.finding: The inference count refers to undefined delta-prime rather than delta-one; the stated G2i induction sequent retains a labelled assumption and does not allow the stipulated empty succedent for falsity.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use delta-one in the count and the unlabelled G2i antecedent with the appropriate translated succedent.

issues.finding: Both examples apply right weakening after an empty-succedent conclusion, producing A on the right although the proposition requires an empty succedent when A is falsity.
issues.proposed_resolution: Retain the empty succedent in both examples; use left weakening only when a disjunction branch lacks a discharged assumption.

issues.location: implication induction step and falsity example
issues.finding: The second induction sequent uses Gamma-one instead of Gamma-two, and the falsity example weakens its second premise to A and concludes A even when the required conclusion is empty. The first premise alone may need right weakening when D is falsity.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use Gamma-two for the second premise, distinguish the translated D and A succedents, weaken only the first premise when D is falsity, and keep the final succedent empty when A is falsity.

issues.finding: For a normal N1i proof with undischarged assumptions, formulas in those assumptions need not be subformulas of the end-formula alone.
issues.proposed_resolution: Include undischarged assumptions alongside the end-formula in the subformula-property statement.

translation_treatment: The target translates the whole section, applies these bounded proof-notation and logic corrections through work/olp0678_source_view.py, and preserves every byte of the frozen English source.
